title: Reason Code 16 — credential mismatch (it's not always the password)
plain_english: NPS matched your policies and got as far as checking the credentials — and the check failed. Either the account name didn't resolve to an account, or the password proof was wrong. This is the single most common NPS reject, and in practice a large share of them are NOT a mistyped password: look at WHICH identity the device actually sent before resetting anything.

causes.cause: A stale saved password on the device — especially after an AD password change, Windows and phones keep sending the cached Wi-Fi credential.
causes.next_check: On the failing device, forget/delete the Wi-Fi network and reconnect entering the current credentials.

causes.cause: Machine vs user authentication mismatch: the User Name field shows 'host/COMPUTER-NAME' (computer auth) while your policy or account expectations assume a user — or the other way round.
causes.next_check: Read the 'User Name' / 'Account Name' fields in this very event: a 'host/' prefix means machine authentication. Align the Wi-Fi profile's authentication mode ('user', 'computer', or 'user or computer') with what your network policy expects.

causes.cause: NTLM hardening broke PEAP-MSCHAPv2: validating the MSCHAPv2 proof needs the NT hash path, and policies disabling NTLM (or Credential Guard on newer Windows) can break it domain-wide.
causes.next_check: Check the domain controller's NTLM audit / 4625 events at the same timestamps; if hardening is the cause, the strategic fix is moving to EAP-TLS rather than re-enabling NTLM.
